name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,650

clue.text: Regret taking away European politician's seat

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so letters are dropped from the word before

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
E is the standard abbreviation for European
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that a European politician has lost their seat in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a parliamentary seat in this political scene, but here it is the body part you sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the hindquarters or buttocks, and seat is a common informal synonym for that part of the body.

clue.text: Judge again concerned with morons' start of sentences

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
asses are fools
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A judge rethinks a ruling about some dim criminals before passing sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom words 'judge' and 'sentences' make a legal picture, but 'Judge again' is simply the definition, and RE is the crossword stock word for 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something is to evaluate it a second time, which is exactly what judging again means.

clue.text: Drink instant tea

blocks.note: a mo is a moment or instant, as in 'half a mo'
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a cup of instant tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like an adjective describing the tea, but it is a noun meaning a moment. Both MO and CHA are informal British words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a coffee drink, often flavoured with chocolate, so it is one example of a drink.

clue.text: Picks pockets craving initially for food

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted
to pocket something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: picks as a noun are selections or choices
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hungry pickpocket steals because they crave something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picks pockets' reads as a thief at work, but 'Picks' is the noun CHOICES and 'pockets' is the container signal. A choc-ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc-ices are frozen dessert bars, a kind of sweet treat you eat, so they count as food in general.

clue.text: Aggressive horde that is surrounding Liberal

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so one part sits inside another

blocks.note: a host is a great crowd or multitude
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: An angry mob closes in around a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horde' suggests a mob, but its job is the old sense of host as a great number, as in 'a host of angels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile and aggressive are synonyms, both describing behaviour that is unfriendly and ready to attack.

clue.text: Typical places where children might play?

definitions.note: plural places described by a phrase naming two of them

blocks.note: first meaning: ordinary, run-of-the-mill
second meaning: a village green or a back yard, two spots for youngsters to run about

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally: a common (public grassland) or a garden is where children play. The question mark flags that this second reading is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something ordinary and unremarkable, so it means typical or everyday in standard British usage.

clue.text: Optimistic about working with female before sign of current depression

blocks.note: c is the abbreviation of circa, about
a machine that is on is working
F is the abbreviation for female
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: A cheerful woman at work is hopeful despite the current economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current depression' sounds like an economic slump, but current is electrical and depression is a physical dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confident means feeling sure things will go well, which is close to an optimistic outlook.

clue.text: Average portion of miso soup

indicators.note: a portion is only part of the whole, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is served an ordinary-sized helping of Japanese miso soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Average portion' reads as a medium serving, but 'portion of' is the signal and 'Average' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so describes something mediocre, neither good nor bad, which matches average in the sense of unremarkable.

clue.text: Carrying out naughty child, lament tone I affected

indicators.note: something affected is altered or put on, so these letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A parent describes having to remove a misbehaving child while adopting a mournful tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying out' looks like physically removing the child, but it is the definition in the sense of executing a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Implementation is the act of putting a plan into effect, which is what carrying out a decision means.

clue.text: Delighted overdue book's lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone missing, so a letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: belated means late or overdue
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A reader is pleased that the overdue library book has gone missing, so no fine.
explanation.walkthrough: BELATED drops its B. 'Book's lost' reads like a lost library book, but book is just the letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means extremely happy and joyful, so it is a direct synonym for being delighted.

clue.text: Whip has compliments about Conservative's deeds

indicators.note: to whip is to beat, as with eggs, so these letters are churned into a new order
about means around, so one part wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A party whip praises a Conservative MP's achievements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like the parliamentary officer who keeps MPs in line, but it is the signal to mix the letters, and the C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplishments are things successfully achieved, and deeds in the sense of notable acts or achievements is a close synonym.

clue.text: Second vehicle left a bike race next to island, notes man?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a composer, a man who writes notes

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a car is a vehicle
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A competitor abandons a second vehicle during a motorbike race held on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing picture fits the Isle of Man TT, which is why 'island' feels part of the scene. 'Notes man?' means someone who writes music.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer famous for keyboard sonatas, so he is a man of musical notes.

clue.text: Strange sacrifices back at home for god

indicators.note: to sacrifice something is to give it up, and here it is the last letter that is surrendered

blocks.note: odd means strange
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Odd sacrificial rites are performed back home in honour of a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacrifices' and 'god' make a religious picture, but sacrifices only signals giving up a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor, so he is a specific example of a god.

clue.text: Crowded square increased in temperature

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for square
something warmed has become hotter

explanation.surface: A packed town square heats up as more people arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowded square' reads as one image, a busy plaza, but 'Crowded' is the definition and 'square' just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to throng or pack a place in large numbers, so swarmed works as a synonym for crowded.

clue.text: See Raab struggling with question put in precarious position?

indicators.note: struggling suggests being in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order
to put something in is to insert it, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
QU is a short form of question

explanation.surface: Watch politician Dominic Raab flounder when a tricky question leaves him exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominic Raab is a former UK Conservative cabinet minister, so the clue reads as political commentary. The position is a ballet pose, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a ballet pose balanced on one leg with the other extended behind, an inherently unsteady stance.

clue.text: Suggested conclusion in article with very reasonable editor

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so only the final letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
V is the abbreviation for very
OK means acceptable or reasonable
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A sensible editor proposes how a newspaper article should end.
explanation.walkthrough: The newsroom picture makes 'conclusion' sound like a story's ending, which in a way it is: the end of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to call it to mind or hint at it, so evoked is a close synonym for suggested.

clue.text: Declares in favour of exams

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour of
tests are exams

explanation.surface: Someone announces support for keeping school examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's usual sense is objection, the opposite of support; here it is the older sense of firmly declaring, as in protesting one's innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest can mean to affirm solemnly, as in protesting your innocence, which matches declaring something.

clue.text: Stopped girl squeezing bottom? On the contrary

indicators.note: squeezing means pressing in, so one part is held inside another
this reverses the roles just described, so the outer and inner parts swap places

blocks.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or the sea
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl was told off for pinching someone's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the girl would hold the bottom; 'On the contrary' flips it so the bottom holds the girl. 'Bottom' is a seabed, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banned is prohibited, so it has been stopped by an authority from happening.

clue.text: Rubbish is said about English flowers

indicators.note: rubbish as an adjective means poor or broken, so these letters must be put right in a new order
about means around, so the mixed letters wrap round another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone claims that English garden blooms are worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish is said' reads like a verdict being given, but 'Rubbish' is the signal to mix the following letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisies are common small white-petalled plants, so they are a familiar example of flowers.

clue.text: Follow tips from sports trainers and reveal heavenly body

indicators.note: the tip of something is its very end, here the front letter of each word

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Taking advice from sports coaches helps someone find a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice and 'trainers' like coaches or shoes; both are just carriers for initial letters. 'and reveal' feels like a link but belongs to the selection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dog Star is Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, so it is a celestial object.

clue.text: Cold in river on Italian craft

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian boat sits on a chilly river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat in this river scene, but it means cunning. The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft in the sense of guile or cunning trickery is a synonym for deceit, as in crafty.

clue.text: Cheese from France went bad on a regular basis

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Cheese imported from France kept going off.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue implies a French cheese, but feta is Greek: 'from France' just supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk, so it is one type of cheese.

clue.text: Wrong rock concert sir succeeded leaving

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
something leaving departs, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to work on
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A knighted rock star wrongly walks out of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock concert' reads as one thing, a gig, but 'rock' is the mixing signal. One S is removed from the letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect and wrong are plain synonyms, both meaning not true or not accurate.

clue.text: This compiler brought up aim to improve

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up turns it upside down so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the setter referring to themselves
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: The setter says their upbringing taught them to strive to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This compiler' is the crossword setter, a common way of saying ME. 'Brought up' sounds like childhood, but it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or revise a text, which makes it better, so it fits improve.

clue.text: Passion reduced with male for company

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: fire is ardour or passion
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Someone's ardour fades once a man is around to keep them company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' sounds like companionship here, but it is a business. FIRE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business organisation, and company is the standard synonym for one.

clue.text: Harry is sensitive in covering Queen's curiosity

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are pushed into a new order
to cover is to wrap around, so the mixed letters enclose another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
QU is a short form of queen

explanation.surface: Prince Harry is touchy about the late Queen's nosiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like Prince Harry in a royal scene with the Queen, but here it is a verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: Inquisitiveness is an eagerness to know things, which is what curiosity means as a noun.

clue.text: Master almost enthusiastic about head's resignation

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the word stops one letter short
about can mean turned round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree
keen means eager or enthusiastic
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is nearly thrilled that the headteacher has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEN loses its N and turns round. 'Head's resignation' suggests a headteacher quitting, but head is a headland and resignation means acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: Resignation in the sense of patient acceptance without complaint is close in meaning to meekness, a mild submissiveness.

clue.text: Basho describes penning poems

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a pen, so the letters are held within the words

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word runs into the second

explanation.surface: The Japanese poet Basho writes about composing his verses.
explanation.walkthrough: Basho was a famous seventeenth-century haiku master, so 'penning poems' reads as writing them. Here 'penning' means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems addressed to a subject, so they are one form of poems in general.
